 GTA 6 Won't Be Released On Disc — Here's What The Physical Copy Contains Instead
 By   Chifundo Kasiya 
 Oct. 27, 2026 11:17 am EST 
 todayyearsold / Instagram 
 Add BGR on Google: 
 Preferred Source 
 Google Discover 
 To say "Grand Theft Auto VI" is an anticipated release that will likely be a cultural and economic event in the games industry is a bit of an understatement. According to BambooHR (via Money ), an HR software company, time off requests for November 19, 2026 (the release date) have spiked by 9% to 17%, and the game is still weeks from release. According to data by Sensor Tower , "GTA 6" has already sold 6.45 million in digital pre-orders, generating an estimated $630 million in revenue.
 Despite this, there's a negative sentiment around physical release for people who value physical ownership of their games. You can buy a physical box for the game, but there's no disc inside. Instead what you get is a download code that you must redeem on the PlayStation or Xbox store in order to claim the digital version of the game. So, the "GTA 6" physical box is only a code in a box. The wild part is that these "physical copies" have managed to sell out at retailers like Amazon at one point in time, as reported by Vice .
 You can get "GTA 6" on Sony PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S , with the Standard Edition and Ultimate Edition costing $79.99 and $99.99, respectively. The physical boxes are only available for the Standard Edition and will be available starting from November 12, 2026 (preloads will also start then). Xbox users can even play it a few hours early using the Xbox New Zealand trick .
 Buying an empty box is a hard sell for some
 Rockstar Games / YouTube 
 Physical and digital games often cost the same, so there's nothing new about the pricing strategy here. However, with "GTA 6" being a code in a box, it loses some of the justifications for dropping full price for a physical edition. Once you redeem that code, it's tied to your PlayStation or Xbox account forever, flying in the face of game preservation and the secondary games market.
 On the game preservation front, "GTA 6" will not be one of those games that make owning an Xbox Series X or PS5 with a disc drive worth it. Some retailers, such as Video Games Plus and Loot Box Gaming , have stated that they will not stock "GTA 6" because it doesn't allow people to truly own what they paid for. Beyond that, should one's PlayStation or Xbox account get banned, cutting off access to all purchased digital games, they will never be able to download their copy of "GTA 6" again. Also, some people buy physical games at full price knowing that they can sell or trade them later, recouping some of the costs to invest in another game.
 So it might be hard to justify buying a physical edition of "GTA 6" unless someone is a hardcore collector. The fact that it's selling out might further hasten the death of physical media in the games industry, especially with Sony's decision to end disc production starting in 2028 .
